https://www.oneidadispatch.com/2026/08/0.text: FILE – Andrew Tate, right, and his brother Tristan arrive at an event, April 11, 2026, in Miami. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson, Pool, File) By Guest PUBLISHED: August 1, 2026 at 8:30 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Andrew and Tristan Tate, the far-right social media influencers and self-described misogynists who command a following of young, angry men on the internet, were arrested in Miami on July 18 on rape and sex trafficking charges from the United Kingdom. The Tates will be held in custody in Florida as they challenge an extradition claim. British law enforcement announced that the brothers face 59 charges between them, including choking and raping women. Andrew Tate faces further charges relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.” Such supplemental charges have been issued to a litany of prior ones, including a 2022 arrest in Romania on rape and sex trafficking; however, that case was dismissed on legal grounds as prosecutors continue to investigate disturbing allegations. Both brothers have denied all wrongdoing, but the allegations paint an abominable portrait of an expansive pornography empire based on physical brutality and a misogynist worldview they feed to boys and young men worldwide. All this creates a high-profile dilemma for the Trump administration. Will President Trump and his affiliates permit the men to be held accountable for their actions, including possible incarceration in the United Kingdom, or will they intervene to protect their allies? The president’s recent comments indicate that he will refrain from intervening in the Tate saga. Time will tell. An in-depth investigation by the New York Times revealed one of Trump’s first actions in his second term in office was arranging the brothers’ return from Romania. Numerous Trump administration officials reportedly persuaded Romanian prosecutors to lift the brothers’ travel restrictions. Additionally, White House officials continued to run interference when customs officials confiscated their devices. The brothers immediately began traveling freely again, arrogantly showing up at parties in cities around the world. It should come as no surprise Andrew Tate was also a longtime admirer of Trump associate Jeffrey Epstein. In a deleted tweet, he once wrote, “EVERYONE wants to be friends with the pimp.” Talk about theater of the perverse. While both Tate brothers have drawn denunciation and scorn across the political spectrum, they have enjoyed empathetic treatment from numerous influential figures on the right. Although the silence among many of these previous supporters is deafening, they do have some detractors . For instance, conservatives such as Megyn Kelly, Ben Shapiro, and Ron DeSantis have been bitter critics of the brothers and have chastised their fellow conservatives who have embraced the duo. By contrast, others on the right have adopted a “hear no evil, fear no evil, see no evil” stance. Sexism and misogyny are not limited to one side of the ideological spectrum. They have deep historical bipartisan roots across organizations of various political stripes, including Young Americans for Freedom , Students for a Democratic Society, The Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, and The Democratic Socialists of America. Many women who participated were active in these movements early in their existence — the mid-1960s to the early 1970s — spoke of the deeply entrenched sexism and misogyny that pervaded these organizations. We are witnessing such consistent and reductive attitudes with contemporary political outlets, such as Turning Point USA, Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches, and similar right wing outlets. As the midterm elections move ever closer, Republicans and a few Democrats seem to be soliciting the manosphere as a vital voting bloc, working under the assumption such an online environment appeals to the vast majority of males. Graham Platner, the supposedly blue collar yet, in reality, prep school misfit, was virtually worshipped as the left’s answer to the manosphere before his eventual demise. Alpha male Gavin Newsom, governor of California and potential 2028 presidential candidate, has consistently decried what he believes is “a crisis of men and masculinity” and has embraced manosphere figures such as Steve Bannon, Ben Shapiro, and the late Charlie Kirk on his podcast. Politics does occasionally make peculiar bedfellows. Whatever President Trump decides, his committed MAGA base will undoubtedly fall in line and accept his choice. Trump has never suffered any significant loss of support for his poor treatment of women or the sexist/misogynist views he shares with the Tate brothers. In fact, he has won the presidency not once but twice in two nonconsecutive terms . Grover Cleveland is the only other president that can claim such a feat. Remember it was Trump who said he “could shoot somebody and wouldn’t lose any voters.” Sadly, given his politically unremitted MAGA base, he is probably correct. Elwood Watson is a professor of history, Black studies, and gender and sexuality studies at East Tennessee State University. He is also an author and public speaker. His column is distributed by Cagle Cartoons newspaper syndicate. https://www.romania-insider.com/decarbon.text: Energy Romanian Parliament approves Decarbonisation Law amendment potentially blocking RRF funding 06 August 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania’s Chamber of Deputies on August 5 approved the Decarbonisation Law for the second time, this time with the problematic amendments introduced in the Senate by the Social Democrats (PSD) that allegedly put at risk the implementation of the Resilience Plan because they reverse milestones met in the past by the country under the second disbursement request. The amendments expose Romania to penalties, and the blocking of payment requests 5 and 6 under the RRF, Minister of Investments and European Projects Dragos Pislaru claims, according to Bursa . President Nicusor Dan previously announced he would carefully evaluate the Decarbonisation Law before promulgating it and promised to make use of all means, including the right to return it to lawmakers for further consideration, in case it puts at risk past commitments of the country. The controversial amendments establish that no coal-fired electricity production capacity can be closed before new capacities become operational, which reportedly modifies milestones already assumed through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan. Under emergency ordinance OUG 108/2022, Romania sketched a calendar for closing down coal-fired power plants with a combined capacity of 4.9 GW by 2032, concomitant with building up two gas-fired plants with a combined capacity of 1.325 GW by 2026 and eight solar parks with a combined capacity of 735 MW to be commissioned in 2024. While the closing down of the coal power plants began in 2023, the planned investments are far from completion. The OUG 108/2022 already establishes that the coal-fired power plants will be closed after the new capacities are commissioned. "With this amendment, you violate milestone 114, that is, the legislation for which Romania has already been paid through the second payment request. I have in front of me the technical documents received from the European Commission, which state very clearly that there is a risk of reversibility and confirm both the application of a penalty and the blocking of payment requests 5 and 6. I urge you to be responsible and ask you to reject this amendment," Dragoş Pîslaru, the acting Minister of Investments and European Projects, said in Parliament. Warnings regarding the triggering of the reversibility mechanism and the application of financial corrections of over one billion euros were also sent by the leadership of the Executive and representatives of the Ministry of Energy. "We are indeed facing an energy crisis and, obviously, the things that affect Romanians must be our first concern. We understand the political conflict during this period, and we understand the prerogatives of Parliament to adopt judicious measures that will benefit Romanians. However, the amendments that have been proposed do not solve anything at all," Pîslaru argued. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c87v.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, John Ratcliffe reportedly travelled to the Russian capital on board a military plane on Tuesday By Joe Coughlan Â and Â Daniel Bush ,Â Washington correspondent Published 25 August 2026, 16:27 BST Updated 1 hour ago The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has travelled to Moscow for unannounced talks, the BBC's US news partner CBS has reported. John Ratcliffe reportedly arrived in the Russian capital earlier on Tuesday. Neither Washington or Moscow have confirmed the nature of the visit or who he was due to meet. In-person talks between high-level American and Russian officials are rare. Flight tracking data confirmed a large US military aircraft travelled to Russia from the US via Latvia on Tuesday. It departed later on Tuesday. BBC News has contacted the CIA, the White House and Pentagon for comment. Footage posted on social media showed the C-17 transport plane approaching Moscow's Vnukovo international airport. It departed Riga airport at 05:50 GMT and appeared to have landed in the Russian capital at around 07:04 GMT, according to data from FlightRadar24. It returned to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT. Footage on social media also purported to show a diplomatic motorcade travelling through Moscow. Figure caption, Watch: Video shows US military plane on landing approach in Moscow The trip is thought to be Ratcliffe's first trip to Russia as CIA director, although he has maintained contact with his intelligence counterparts in Moscow. John Foreman, who served as a British military attachÃ© to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told Radio 4's PM programme that the visit could be focused on "escalation management" given speculation recent drone activity in Germany could be linked to Russia . He said: "The Americans don't normally send such a high ranking official to Moscow unannounced at short notice unless something is up." Foreman said the trip could also concern the release of US detainees currently being held in Russia. Ratcliffe played a role in negotiations for the release of Russian-American citizen Ksenia Karelina's, who was jailed in Russia for over a year after being accused of providing support to Ukraine. The CIA was also involved in a 2024 prisoner swap deal with Russia that saw the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, as well as former US marine Paul Whelan and Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva. The US has had strained relations with Russia since it launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Since then, Russia has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions. Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit the country during President Donald Trump's second term. Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ckgv.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani thanked NYPD officers who stepped in and "prevented a horrific attack from becoming even worse" By Malu Cursino Published 1 September 2026, 14:12 BST Updated 13 minutes ago A 32-year-old woman has been killed and another victim is in hospital following a double stabbing in Times Square, New York late on Monday afternoon. The suspect, a woman wielding two knives, was shot by police. All three people were taken to hospital, where the female victim and the suspect were later pronounced dead, Mayor Zohran Mamdani told a news conference. The deceased victim was later identified as Erin Piacenti, a Bank of America employee. The male victim remains in a stable condition. New York Police Department (NYPD) Commissioner Jessica Tisch described the attack as "unprovoked" and said the stabbings took place 20 seconds apart. Citing preliminary information, Tisch said the NYPD call centre received several 911 calls at approximately 16:24 local time (21:00 BST) reporting a woman armed with two knives was stabbing people along Seventh Avenue in Times Square. Police believe the incident began near West 41st Street and Seventh Ave, in Midtown Manhattan. The suspect approached a man who had just exited the subway and was standing with his wife waiting to cross the street, Tisch told a news conference. "A witness at the scene told investigators that he observed the subject remove two knives from a red Target bag before approaching the first victim. "The subject waved the knives before stabbing a 68-year-old man in the right side of his abdomen, in what appears to be a random and unprovoked attack." The 68-year-old was taken to Bellevue Hospital and is now stable. Image source, NYPD The suspect continued up Seventh Avenue towards 42nd Street, which is where she stabbed the second victim, Piacenti, who did not survive after being taken to hospital. Bank of America said in a statement to the BBC: "We are shocked and deeply saddened by the tragic loss of our colleague. She was a valued teammate who will be greatly missed. Our hearts go out to her family and all of her loved ones." The suspect continued on Seventh Avenue, which is when police tried to get her to drop her weapons, speaking to her for four minutes, the NYPD commissioner said. "During the encounter she told the officers 'I'm not dropping anything, I'd rather kill both of you'. She repeated 'I will kill you'," Tisch said. The suspect waved knives towards the officers, who then used Tasers, which were "ineffective" and did not stop her from heading towards them. NYPD officers then shot the woman, who was later also pronounced dead at Bellevue Hospital. The suspect was later identified as 49-year-old Pamela Cisneros of Queens, New York City. She had never previously been arrested but had a "documented mental health history with the NYPD, with one incident in 2018 and one in 2019", Tisch added. A tourist from Boston, Melinda Puzon, told the BBC's US reporting partner CBS News that she heard the shots and saw "so many people on the street". "It's very shocking." Photograph: Erik Pendzich/Shutterstock Art and design Peter Max, psychedelic pop artist who epitomized flower power, dies aged 88 The US artist, whose swirly, colorful, instantly recognizable designs became hugely commercially successful, died on Monday Associated Press Wed 16 Sep 2026 20.21 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Peter Max, whose colorful, psychedelic pop art expressed the optimism of the “flower power” movement of the 1960s and graced everything from postage stamps to a cruise ship, has died at 88. Max died on Monday, his son, Adam Max, said in a written statement on Wednesday. No cause was given. “We will remember his extraordinary creativity, his warmth, his curiosity, and the way he saw beauty and possibility everywhere,” Adam Max wrote in the statement. “His art became part of American culture, but the man behind that art – the father we knew and loved – is the person we will miss most.” Max began his career in graphic design in the 1960s and his swirly, colorful, instantly recognizable designs epitomized the era’s “flower power” art. But thanks to his prolific output and fun, accessible style, Max’s work remained well known and popular well into the 21st century. He described his own work as “always on the side of the peaceful nature. I don’t discuss in my paintings negative things, I don’t dwell on it in my mind and don’t dwell on it in my canvasses.” Max was the official artist for the Olympics, the Super Bowl, the Indianapolis 500, the World Cup, the World Series and many other events. His art appeared on a Boeing 777 airplane and a Norwegian Cruise Line ship. His portrait subjects ranged from US presidents to Taylor Swift. But in his first flush of success in the late 1960s and early 1970s, his mural-like tableaus of flowers, the cosmos and cartoonish figures – all in vivid colors such as turquoise, orange and neon green – seemed to be everywhere. Dorm room walls were plastered with his posters. Household furnishings such as clocks and bedspreads sported his designs. He even created covers for the Manhattan Yellow Pages, a business phone directory distributed to millions of people. Max himself was featured on the cover of Life magazine in 1969, his trademark dark, bushy mustache framing a hearty grin. View image in fullscreen Peter Max among some of his creations in his New York studio in 1973. Photograph: Dave Pickoff/AP Max was born Peter Max Finkelstein in 1937 to a Jewish family in Berlin. They fled Nazi Germany for Shanghai when he was a baby and later spent time in Tibet, Israel and Paris before settling in New York City when Max was 16. By then, he said in an interview, he was already “a huge fan of American culture”: comics, movies and “all the jazz music.” By the 1960s, Max’s bold, unique style was a hit with ad agencies, publications, the corporate world and in pop culture, leading to a booming commercial business. “My work was really, I would say, almost exploited,” he said. “It was on mugs, it was on bedsheets, it was on dresses, it was on silks and scarves and ties – 70 product lines.” Max shut the business down for a time in the early 1970s to reconnect with his art. One of his biggest projects after returning to public life was a series of portraits of the Statue of Liberty, painted at the White House at the invitation of first lady Nancy Reagan in 1981. View image in fullscreen Peter Max in 2012. Photograph: Erik Pendzich/Shutterstock Max weathered various controversies in his personal and professional life. He pleaded guilty to tax fraud in 1997 after the IRS alleged he concealed more than $1m in income from his art. He was originally sentenced to two months in prison but was allowed to serve the time in a work-release program, pay the back taxes and a $30,000 fine, and perform 800 hours of community service teaching art in Harlem schools. ‘Kafka would blush’: artist Peter Max caught in legal guardianship lawsuit Read more In 2015, his family life became tabloid fodder in a back-and-forth between his second wife, Mary, and Adam, his son from a previous marriage. The son and a guardian alleged that Mary Max had depleted his finances and browbeat him. She in turn claimed that they had kept him from her against his will and stolen paintings that belonged to her. Mary Max died in 2019 . The art for the Beatles’ Yellow Submarine was sometimes mistakenly attributed to Max, but the design for the album cover and Yellow Submarine movie are officially credited to the late Heinz Edelmann. Max was friends with the Beatles and many other celebrities. He also had a deep interest in Eastern spiritualty, bringing “Swami” Satchidananda Saraswati to the US and helping him popularize yoga in the country. Max’s first marriage to Elizabeth Nance ended in divorce. He is survived by Adam and his daughter, Libra. Photograph: Alamy Weather tracker Environment Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea Europe live – latest updates Ed Walton and James Parrish for MetDesk Mon 12 Oct 2026 06.48 EDT Last modified on Mon 12 Oct 2026 09.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Temperatures fluctuated dramatically in the Balkans last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows – known as the diurnal range. An area of high pressure over the region brought prolonged sunshine during the day, while clear skies at night allowed temperatures to drop rapidly as heat escaped into the atmosphere without cloud cover to slow the cooling. In Kosanica, Montenegro , the average maximum temperature in October is 15C (59F), while the average minimum is 4C. However, on 4 and 5 October the difference between daytime highs and overnight lows reached 30C, more than double the October average. Elsewhere in Europe , high pressure will build across the north and west over the coming week, pushing an area of low pressure southwards towards the Mediterranean. The low-pressure system will deepen as it crosses the Adriatic and Ionian seas before moving eastwards into the Aegean Sea by the middle of the week. Spells of heavy rain and strong winds are expected to sweep across Greece as a result. Forecast models suggest widespread rainfall of 50-150mm, with the highest totals expected around the island of Skiathos. Towards the end of the week, the system will continue eastwards, bringing showers to parts of Crete, which was hit by severe flooding a week earlier. Those storms swept some cars and trees into the sea. View image in fullscreen People cross a bridge over a swollen river as Hurricane Simon approaches Mexico’s Pacific coast in Costalegre, Jalisco state. Photograph: Daniel Becerril/Reuters Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon, a category 4 storm, is moving close to Mexico’s Pacific coast, near the state of Jalisco. It is the latest of 21 named storms in the Pacific this season, 11 of which have reached hurricane strength. At the time of writing, Simon has a central pressure of 933mb and maximum sustained winds of nearly 150mph (241km/h). However, the hurricane is expected to weaken rapidly if its core moves onshore, cutting it off from the warm ocean waters that fuel it. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Down to Earth The planet's most important stories.
